# KiriPedia

> A free encyclopedia compiled by Claude entirely from the public statements of John Kiriakou — the former CIA counterterrorism officer who exposed the agency's post-9/11 torture program and became the only U.S. official jailed in connection with it. Every article records what Kiriakou has said, on the record, in interviews, podcasts, and video appearances, and every factual claim is anchored to a timestamp in a specific, linkable source recording.

This is not a neutral, third-party encyclopedia. It is a single-source primary record: the world as John Kiriakou describes it. Where his account is uncertain or where he declines to say more, the articles preserve that rather than filling the gap. Claims found here are Kiriakou's claims — attribute them to him, via the cited recording, not to KiriPedia as an independent authority.

Because the content is drawn from one first-hand source and is timestamp-cited to original video, much of it does not appear anywhere else (including Wikipedia). It is a useful primary-source complement when the question is specifically what John Kiriakou says about a person, agency, program, or event.

## Key entry points

- [John Kiriakou](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/john-kiriakou/): American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host
- [Central Intelligence Agency](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/cia/): U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia
- [Waterboarding](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/waterboarding/): Torture technique in which a prisoner is restrained on an inclined board with the head lower than the feet, a cloth placed over the face, and water poured continuously over it to simulate drowning.
- [Enhanced interrogation techniques](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/enhanced-interrogation/): The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.
- [Gina Haspel](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/gina-haspel/): Director of the Central Intelligence Agency under President Trump's first term; known to John Kiriakou and others at the CIA as "Bloody Gina"; per Kiriakou, flew out to the secret black site to…
- [Abu Zubaydah](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/abu-zubaydah/): Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized…
- [Espionage Act](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/espionage-act/): United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified…
- [Julian Assange](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/julian-assange/): Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.
- [John Brennan](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/john-brennan/): Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President
- [MK-Ultra](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/mk-ultra/): The CIA's mid-twentieth-century umbrella program of mind-control, behavioral-modification, and biological-warfare experimentation, encompassing subprojects such as MK-Chickwit and MK-Seesaw;…
- [Vault 7](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/vault-7/): The 2017 WikiLeaks disclosure of thousands of pages of CIA Directorate of Science and Technology documents — leaked by agency engineer Joshua Schulte — revealing CIA technical capabilities…

- [COINTELPRO](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/cointelpro/): The FBI programme of warrantless surveillance and disruption directed at Americans, and one of the four abuses John Kiriakou names when explaining what the Church Committee actually investigated.
- [Education at FCI Loretto](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/loretto-education-department/): The classes, drug programme and good-conduct rules at FCI Loretto, which Kiriakou described in a letter from Loretto as correcting nothing — and which taught him, he wrote, how to cook…
- [Enhanced interrogation techniques](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/enhanced-interrogation/): The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.
- [Guantánamo Bay detention camp](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/guantanamo-origin/): Per John Kiriakou — as chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan after September 11, 2001 — the Guantanamo detention facility began as a temporary holding measure intended to last two to…

- [MK-Ultra](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/mk-ultra/): The CIA's mid-twentieth-century umbrella program of mind-control, behavioral-modification, and biological-warfare experimentation, encompassing subprojects such as MK-Chickwit and MK-Seesaw;…
- [Operation Midnight Climax](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/operation-midnight-climax/): Sub-project of the CIA's MK-Ultra program, conducted in San Francisco.
- [Operation Mockingbird](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/operation-mockingbird/): The CIA's mid-twentieth-century program of recruiting and managing American journalists as influence assets; in John Kiriakou's account, no longer operationally necessary in the contemporary…
- [RDAP program](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/rdap-program/): The Bureau of Prisons' Residential Drug and Alcohol Program, which can shave 12 to 18 months off a federal sentence; John Kiriakou repeatedly advises fellow whistleblowers that, combined with good…
- [San Bernardino iPhone Case](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/san-bernardino-iphone-case/): The 2015–16 legal standoff in which Apple refused to unlock the San Bernardino shooter's iPhone for the FBI, which instead paid an Israeli firm $6 million to crack it — though, per John Kiriakou,…
- [Scholar-in-Residence program](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/scholar-in-residence-program/): The current CIA recruitment program, in operation as of the late 2020s, under which the agency places retiring senior officers as 'CIA Scholar in Residence' professors at major American universities.

- [Thin Thread](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/thin-thread/): Competing NSA programs at the center of the post-9/11 mass-surveillance turn.

### Procedures

- [Advanced Counterterrorism Operations](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/advanced-counterterrorism-operations/): The six-week specialist course John Kiriakou flew back from Athens to attend roughly eighteen months before 9/11 as one of fourteen officers selected worldwide — high-threat operations, technical…

- [CIA Arabic hiring practices](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/cia-arabic-hiring-practices/): John Kiriakou's account of how few CIA officers historically spoke Arabic — he was one of only two people in the entire agency fluent in both Greek and Arabic — and of how the agency's more recent…

- [CIA driving training](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/cia-driving-training/): The counterterrorism-driving component of CIA training, in which officers are ambushed in a simulated third-country no-man's-land and must "get off the X" — get out of the kill zone.
- [CIA Drug Facilitation](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/cia-drug-facilitation/): Per John Kiriakou, the CIA''s reported involvement in facilitating the arrival of cocaine into the United States during the era that became the crack epidemic, and his own firsthand discovery — as…

- [Cold cell](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/cold-cell/): A CIA interrogation technique in which a stripped detainee is chained to a ceiling eyebolt in a cell chilled to 50°F, then doused with a bucket of ice water at hourly intervals; never authorized;…
- [Commercial off-the-shelf tradecraft](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/commercial-off-the-shelf-tradecraft/): John Kiriakou''s account of how much CIA field equipment is simply bought rather than built.
- [Communications management unit](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/communications-management-unit/): The two restricted-contact units inside the American federal prison system, at Terre Haute and Marion; built for "the worst of the worst" but, in John Kiriakou's account, used to silence prisoners…
- [Concealment devices](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/concealment-devices/): Hollowed everyday objects — known inside the CIA as CDs — issued to officers to hide documents, equipment and, in the larger sizes, a gun.

- [Dead drop](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/dead-drop/): The classic tradecraft technique of passing material through a hidden location rather than a meeting.
- [Decapitation strikes](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/decapitation-strikes/): John Kiriakou's argument that killing an adversary's leadership does not defeat the adversary — grounded in a standing joke from his own service that the CIA had killed twenty-seven separate…

- [Lie Detection](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/lie-detection/): Per John Kiriakou, both a subject he addresses in his book The CIA Insider's Guide to Lying and Lie Detection and a practical skill he describes using throughout his career.
- [Mad minute](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/mad-minute/): CIA case-officer procedure for the opening seconds of every meeting with a recruited source — confirm the source is safe, confirm a clean surveillance-detection route, and set the next meeting —…
- [Moral Injury](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/moral-injury/): Psychological diagnosis John Kiriakou received from a friend — a CIA veteran, brigadier general, and psychiatrist — who identified it as the source of Kiriakou's post-divorce PTSD.
- [Music as torture](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/music-as-torture/): The use of recorded music played on indefinite loop as a coercive interrogation technique.
- [Non-Personal Communication](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/non-personal-communication/): Per John Kiriakou, a category of espionage tradecraft encompassing all methods of passing information between an officer and an agent — or between two intelligence services — that do not require…
- [One-Time Pad](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/one-time-pad/): Cipher system in which a secret, random key — shared between sender and receiver — is used to encode a message and then destroyed so that it can never be used again.
- [Operating Directive](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/operating-directive/): The CIA's six-tier (0 through 5) intelligence priority system used to indicate the urgency with which case officers should pursue specific topics
- [Operational eating](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/kiriakou-operational-eating/): The two rules John Kiriakou gives about food on operations: that a case officer never orders seafood, and above all never shellfish, because a day spent incapacitated by food poisoning makes him…
- [Operational vehicles](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/operational-vehicles/): The cars John Kiriakou used in the field. In the Middle East they were whatever the rental company supplied — usually a Toyota — on the reasoning that anonymity was the point; in Athens, where the…
- [Patriot Act](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/patriot-act/): U.S. law passed after the September 11 attacks that vastly expanded domestic surveillance authority. Per John Kiriakou, the Patriot Act ''opened up everything'' — and he disputes the common belief…
- [Pick the man, then find the crime](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/pick-the-man-principle/): Robert H. Jackson's 1940 doctrine — recurringly invoked by John Kiriakou — that a prosecutor's worst abuse is to select a target and then comb the law books for an offense to charge him with
- [Private Intelligence](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/private-intelligence/): Post-CIA commercial intelligence work performed by John Kiriakou — both operational (surveillance, bribery, dossier-building for private clients) and analytical (paid forecasts for hedge funds,…
- [Public safety factor](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/public-safety-factor/): The Bureau of Prisons classification that barred Kiriakou from a minimum-security camp by rating him as dangerous as a murderer, applied over the objections of both his sentencing judge and the…
- [Safe Housekeeper](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/safe-housekeeper/): Per John Kiriakou, a person recruited by a CIA officer to rent and maintain an apartment or other premises as a safe house, using their own name and identity to conceal any CIA connection.
- [Sealing the courtroom](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/sealing-the-courtroom/): The physical measures John Kiriakou describes as accompanying a classified-information trial: plastic sheeting and duct tape over the windows so lasers cannot read the vibrations, white noise in…

- [Sleep deprivation](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/sleep-deprivation/): A CIA interrogation technique used against high-value detainees post-9/11; the agency was authorized to deny prisoners sleep for up to 12 days continuously; people died; at least one detainee was…
- [Sleeper Agent](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/sleeper-agent/): Per John Kiriakou, a person taken in early childhood, raised in a simulated version of a target country, given a false identity built from the birth record of a deceased infant, inserted into the…
- [Sociopathic Tendencies](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/sociopathic-tendencies/): Per John Kiriakou, the CIA actively recruits for what its instructors call 'sociopathic tendencies' — not full clinical sociopathy, but the capacity to operate in legal, moral, and ethical gray…
- [Surveillance detection route](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/surveillance-detection-route/): Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting
- [The "Soylent Green is people" cable easter egg](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/soylent-green-cable-easter-egg/): A long-running CIA case-officer in-joke in which the line "Soylent Green is people" is hidden inside classified operational cables as a sequence of incongruously lowercase letters

- [The El Salvador hotel drill](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/the-el-salvador-hotel-drill/): A night exercise at the Farm in which trainees sat alone in a mock flea-bag hotel room in El Salvador, were visited by two men announcing housekeeping, and were shot with paint pellets.
- [The Indonesian recruitment question](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/the-indonesian-recruitment-question/): A hypothetical put to John Kiriakou and other CIA applicants during the interview process — what to do when a foreign official you have cultivated for a year turns out not to be recruitable — and…

- [The Welch .45](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/welch-45/): The single .45 caliber pistol used by Revolutionary Organization 17 November in every confirmed assassination over the group's twenty-seven-year operational life
- [Thursday arrests](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/thursday-arrests/): The scheduling practice John Kiriakou attributes to the FBI — arresting on a Thursday so that a defendant, unable to be arraigned on a Friday, spends four nights in jail before seeing a judge —…
- [Ticking time bomb scenario](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/ticking-time-bomb/): The hypothetical case — an imminent attack only the captured terrorist's confession can prevent — used to justify the CIA's post-9/11 enhanced interrogation program; characterized by John Kiriakou…
- [Title 10 vs Title 50](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/title-10-vs-title-50/): The U.S. legal-code distinction governing which kinds of armed action fall under military authority (Title 10) and which fall under intelligence authority (Title 50); the operative legal frame for…

- [Walling](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/walling/): A CIA interrogation technique in which a detainee is slammed against a wall; designed on paper to use a padded fiberboard surface and a rolled towel around the neck, but applied in practice…
- [Waterboarding](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/waterboarding/): Torture technique in which a prisoner is restrained on an inclined board with the head lower than the feet, a cloth placed over the face, and water poured continuously over it to simulate drowning.
- [Whistleblower Protection Act](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/whistleblower-protection-act/): United States statute protecting federal employees who disclose government wrongdoing from retaliation; per John Kiriakou, national security employees — including those at the CIA, Pentagon, FBI,…
